stemMd: A transportation agency selected $120$ commuters at random from all the commuters in a city and recorded each one's one-way commute time. The mean commute time for the sample was $34$ minutes, with an associated margin of error of $2.5$ minutes. Which of the following is a plausible value for the mean one-way commute time, in minutes, of all commuters in the city?
explanationMd:
A margin of error gives a range of plausible values for the population mean: the sample mean minus the margin to the sample mean plus the margin.

$$34 - 2.5 = 31.5 \qquad 34 + 2.5 = 36.5$$

So plausible values for the mean commute time of all the city's commuters run from $31.5$ to $36.5$ minutes. Of the values offered, only $35$ lies in that range.

Check the others against the endpoints: $31$ is below $31.5$, $37$ is above $36.5$, and $39$ is well above it. The value $39$ comes from adding the margin of error twice ($34 + 5$), which doubles the width of the range.

distractorRationale.a: The lower end of the plausible range is $34 - 2.5 = 31.5$, and $31$ is below it; this comes from rounding the margin up to $3$ before subtracting.
distractorRationale.c: The upper end of the plausible range is $34 + 2.5 = 36.5$, and $37$ is above it; this comes from rounding the margin up to $3$ before adding.
distractorRationale.d: This adds the margin of error twice, $34 + 2(2.5) = 39$. The plausible range extends only one margin of error on each side of the sample mean, up to $36.5$.

accessibilityText: A random sample of 120 of a city's commuters had a mean one-way commute time of 34 minutes, with a margin of error of 2.5 minutes. Which is a plausible value, in minutes, for the mean commute time of all the city's commuters? The choices are 31, 35, 37 and 39.

provenance.notes: Original item. Builds the plausible interval for a population mean from a sample mean and margin of error, with distractors just outside each endpoint.
